title: Cedar Falls Rising
premise: August Fairweather has survived two years at Cedar Falls Academy by being unremarkable—until their best friend Theo vanishes overnight, leaving behind a ring of keys stamped with the academy's founding year. Following the keys, August uncovers the Ledger, a century-old game of favors and debts that quietly runs the town, and learns Theo was trying to end it. As August is pulled into the final round before the season's last game, they must decide whether to protect the tradition that gives Cedar Falls its identity or burn it down knowing the town may not survive the truth. In the end, August wins the game only to refuse its prize, exposing the Ledger publicly and choosing a harder, honest belonging over the safety of invisibility.
about_author: G. M. Winterbourne grew up in a small mill town where everyone knew everyone's business and half of it wasn't true. They write stories about sharp-edged kids who learn that fitting in and belonging are not the same thing.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Unremarkable
chapters.summary: August's POV. A tour of Cedar Falls Academy through August's careful strategy of invisibility: keep grades solid, opinions smaller, friendships to exactly one person—Theo. The chapter ends with Theo promising to show August something 'that explains everything' after the pep rally. Emotional beat: uneasy comfort, the sense that fine is a performance.

chapters.title: Empty Bed, Full Silence
chapters.summary: August's POV. Theo doesn't come home; his mother assumes he's at August's. All that remains is a set of antique keys on August's desk with no note. The school closes ranks suspiciously fast, and Headmaster Voss gently suggests Theo ran away. Emotional beat: fear curdling into the first flicker of defiance.

chapters.title: Keys to the Founders' Floor
chapters.summary: August's POV. One key opens a sealed wing beneath the library—the Founders' Archive—where August finds the Ledger: a leather book recording decades of 'favors' owed between town families and the academy. Theo's name appears in fresh ink, marked 'called in.' Emotional beat: vertigo; the town August knew was a stage set.

chapters.title: Everyone Owes Someone
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Priya Chandrasekaran, student council president and reluctant Ledger insider. She warns August off but lets slip that the game is real, seasonal, and that this year's final round falls on the last football game. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two people who trust no one trusting each other slightly.

chapters.title: What Theo Was Building
chapters.summary: August's POV. Following Theo's trail through borrowed library slips and a storage unit key, August finds his hidden research: proof that the Ledger's debts were engineered to trap scholarship families like theirs. Theo meant to publish it. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose—August stops searching for Theo and starts finishing his work.

chapters.title: An Offer Wrapped in Kindness
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The headmaster offers August a full ride, a future, and Theo's safe return—all in exchange for the keys and silence. He frames it as protection, and worst of all, part of August wants to believe him. Emotional beat: temptation; power offering itself as rescue.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya reveals her own family's crushing entry in the Ledger and confesses she was assigned to watch August. Together they decode the rules: the final game is a public ritual where debts are settled or forgiven by whoever holds the Ledger. Emotional beat: shared shame transformed into shared resolve.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: August's POV. August leaks fragments of the Ledger online, forcing the town into open panic days before the championship. Voss accelerates the ritual, and August realizes the game can't be stopped from outside—it must be won. Theo's last note surfaces: 'Win it, then break it.' Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: August's POV, halftime climax. Under stadium lights, before the whole town, August plays the final round against Voss—wagers, debts, and Theo's fate on the table—and wins by invoking a founder's clause Voss never expected. Offered the Ledger itself, August refuses it and reads the debts aloud instead. Emotional beat: triumph that costs everything comfortable.

chapters.title: Cedar Falls Rising
chapters.summary: August's POV, weeks later. Theo is found alive, changed and ashamed; the Ledger is public record, the academy under reform, the town furious and grieving and, slowly, talking honestly for the first time. August is no longer invisible—and discovers being seen is survivable. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging, chosen over safety.
